name: Methylprednisolone
sections: White, odourless crystalline powder; melting point 228–237 °C; practically insoluble in water.
Synthesised and manufactured by Upjohn; on the WHO List of Essential Medicines (as the sodium succinate injection). First approval/introduction: US FDA October 1957 (The Upjohn Company).

Synthetic glucocorticoid with potent anti-inflammatory and immunosuppressive activity and minimal mineralocorticoid effect. 4 mg methylprednisolone ≈ 5 mg prednisolone. Receptor / target profile: Glucocorticoid receptor agonist with minimal mineralocorticoid activity; 4 mg ≈ 5 mg prednisolone.
Summary: Bioavailability ~88%; Tmax ~1.5 h. Hepatic metabolism (CYP3A4). Plasma half-life ~2.5 h; biological half-life 12–36 h.
Rheumatic disorders – RA, polymyalgia rheumatica, SLE, vasculitis
Allergic states – severe asthma, allergic rhinitis, drug reactions
Respiratory, renal (nephrotic syndrome), haematological, GI (IBD) and neurological (MS relapse) disorders
Initial dose 4–48 mg/day depending on condition and severity
Adjust to the lowest effective maintenance dose
Single morning dose (after breakfast) minimises adrenal suppression; alternate-day therapy for long-term use
Taper gradually after more than 3 weeks of therapy
Dose to be individualised by the treating physician according to clinical response and tolerability.
Enhanced effect in cirrhosis – may need dose reduction.
Osteoporosis, diabetes, hypertension risk – lowest effective dose.
Excreted in milk; acceptable at low doses.
Adrenal suppression – taper after prolonged use
Infections – TB reactivation, masking of infection
BP, glucose, weight, electrolytes, bone density, eye examination, growth.
Established efficacy across inflammatory and autoimmune disorders; high-dose pulses used in MS relapses, lupus nephritis and vasculitis.
Take in the morning after breakfast
Do not stop suddenly after long-term use
Carry a steroid card if on long-term therapy
Store below 30°C in a dry place, protected from light and moisture. Keep out of the reach of children. Do not use after the expiry date.
